feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital/public-sector communications roles: the positioning is clear, the experience shows progression, and the scope feels substantive. Writing is polished overall, but the document is somewhat dense and repetitive, with a few style/grammar inconsistencies that reduce sharpness.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear senior-level brand: the headline, summary, and career progression strongly support “Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader.”  
- Good credibility through scale and specificity: 10,000+ pages, 3.5M annual page views, 50+ publishers, named tools/platforms, and concrete project examples.  
- Broad yet coherent scope across strategy, governance, analytics, CMS, multimedia, and AI-enabled search, which makes the profile distinctive.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication across Core Competencies, Topline Skills, Technical + IT, and project descriptions; consolidate to create a tighter, more scannable CV.  
- Add more outcome-focused impact beyond responsibilities: include measurable results for newsletters, social growth, campaign performance, efficiency gains, adoption, or stakeholder outcomes.  
- Fix minor style/grammar issues: “social, and multimedia” should be “social and multimedia”; “A2/Learning” is stylistically awkward; punctuation/hyphenation is inconsistent (e.g., “organization-wide,” “member-facing,” “front-end,” date abbreviations, and list formatting). No obvious misspellings found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary with clear seniority and domain focus. It’s polished, but slightly broad and overlaps with competencies/work experience; adding one concrete scale cue would increase impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten and make more specific: “Digital platform and communications leader with 12+ years’ experience modernizing enterprise web ecosystems, governance models, and content operations for high-volume public-sector organizations.”
- Add a scale/result cue drawn from recent work, e.g. “including a 10,000+ page Drupal migration supporting 3.5M annual page views.”
- Replace “Leads” with a parallel noun/verb structure for smoother style: “Expertise spans enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial governance, multimedia production, and AI-enabled search/content experiences.”
- Consider aligning wording with the subtitle: use “digital platform & communications systems leader” or “enterprise digital leader” for consistency.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Governance models/content operations” and the capability list repeat Core Competencies and Topline Skills closely.
- “AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps with recent projects; “AI-enabled search and content experiences” would be more precise.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Technical + IT sections. It would be stronger if tightened to emphasize strategic capability areas rather than repeating detailed skill phrases.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use broader, cleaner categories to reduce repetition and improve scanability.
- Prioritize the most senior/recent strengths: web modernization, governance, analytics, AI/search, and cross-channel operations.
- Standardize phrasing for parallel structure; avoid mixing systems, functions, and outputs in one list.
- Suggested rewrite: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, reporting, and optimization • Cross-channel communications leadership • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Public-sector and advocacy communications • Multimedia and livestream production

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled search and content experiences” overlaps with header, recent projects, and Topline Skills.
- “Multimedia production and livestream operations” is already covered in Topline Skills and multiple roles.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshots that reinforce the CV’s themes, but the block is too dense and repeats points already covered in Work Experience. Tightening wording and emphasizing outcomes or distinct scope will improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add dates or “Selected Recent Projects” framing, and use parallel verb-led structure for each item.
- Tighten phrasing: “hybrid retrieval, vector search, and bill-level AI chat” is clearer than “combining…”
- Prioritize what is unique to each project: AI search architecture, Drupal 10 microsite build, conference installation, recurring video program.
- If possible, add one concrete result, audience, or scale metric to 1–2 projects.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite work, and advocacy video series substantially overlap with the current freelance and NACo experience bullets.
- “Editorial storytelling,” “production and distribution,” and “campaign growth” are somewhat generic; sharpen or cut if space is tight.

items.title: Coleman Davis
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email
items.content: colemandavis4@gmail.com

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear relevance, but it reads broad and overlaps heavily with the header, competencies, and NACo entries. Tighten it around distinctive consulting impact, platform execution, and the AI search initiative.

Suggested edit
- Open with scope + client type + outcomes: “Embedded full-time as strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital platform improvements, campaign delivery, and content operations.”
- Replace generic verbs with sharper ownership: “Built”/“Led”/“Implemented” instead of “Support”/“Advise”/“Deliver.”
- Consolidate into 4–5 bullets and add metrics where possible: number of sites/pages, users, publishers, campaign launches, toolkit downloads, workflow time saved, search accuracy/engagement gains.
- Make the AI work a flagship bullet: “Led AI-enabled search initiative across retrieval design, structured content workflows, and discovery UX for complex policy/member content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Governance, workflows, analytics, and enterprise web improvement” repeats language already used in the summary and NACo roles.
- The microsite/toolkit work overlaps with Recent Projects; keep this entry focused on role-level ownership, not project detail.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale signals. It will be sharper if you reduce channel-overview wording, foreground the biggest outcomes, and avoid repeating responsibilities covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a tighter scope/outcome line: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget for a high-volume public-sector communications operation.”
- Prioritize the most distinctive wins first: website migration, analytics stack expansion, and in-house studio build.
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: team size, budget, email list size/open rates, social growth, reporting efficiency, production cost savings, or faster publishing workflows.
- Rewrite bullets to be action + result focused, e.g. “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal site serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ publishers.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this entry focused on enterprise leadership and transformation.
- Governance/publishing standards language may duplicate the header and consulting role unless tied to a specific operational result.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more clearly about executional leadership, channel growth, and cross-team coordination at this stage.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead to emphasize scope and level: “Managed day-to-day digital communications operations across NACo’s web, email, social and video channels, supporting advocacy messaging and organization-wide editorial coordination.”
- Tighten bullets and foreground outcomes: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more active and distinct: “Launched and produced a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine the last two bullets into one stronger systems point: “Improved editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, increasing consistency and coordination.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Helped scale” and “helped improve” sound vague; use direct ownership where accurate.
- Avoid repeating website, governance, analytics, and studio-building themes already covered more strongly in the Director role.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. Make it sharper, more senior, and tied to the candidate’s recent enterprise/public-sector leadership.

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad phrases with tighter, differentiated wording:
- Enterprise digital strategy for public-sector organizations
- Editorial governance and content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Advocacy and member-facing messaging
- Audience-centered content strategy
- Consider adding one higher-impact phrase drawn from recent work, e.g. “Enterprise web modernization leadership” or “AI-enabled content discovery strategy.”
- Keep wording noun-based and parallel; avoid mixing “leadership,” “messaging,” and “planning” without a consistent structure.
- If space allows, prioritize governance, modernization, and content operations over “audience-focused content planning,” which feels less senior.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “editorial systems and governance,” and “multi-channel communications” duplicate Core Competencies almost exactly.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” also repeats language already established in the header and work experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill coverage, but this item is too long and overlaps heavily with the separate “Technical + IT” section. As a topline skills entry, it should be tighter, more strategic, and emphasize the most relevant recent strengths.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tool dump to capability-led grouping: “Drupal and CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Drop lower-priority or older-platform mentions here, especially jQuery; keep detailed platform inventory in “Technical + IT.”
- Consider removing WordPress, SharePoint, and Power Pages from this topline item unless they are central to current target roles; Drupal is the strongest recent signal.
- If you want one stronger version: “Drupal-led web modernization • Front-end web implementation • API and workflow integrations • Airtable systems • AI-enabled search”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates “Technical + IT > Web Platforms & CMS” and “Coding & Technical Implementation.”
- “CMS modernization,” “workflow automation,” and “AI-enabled search experiences” also echo Core Competencies; keep wording distinct.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” analytics section and reads as a tool list rather than a senior, outcome-oriented capability summary. In Topline Skills, emphasize decision-making and optimization leadership over platforms alone.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-first to capability-first, e.g.: “Analytics strategy • KPI framework design • Executive dashboarding and leadership reporting • Web performance and SEO analysis • User behavior insights (GA4, Clarity) • BI and data visualization (Looker Studio, Power BI, BigQuery)”
- Group tools in parentheses instead of listing each as separate bullets to improve concision and seniority.
- Replace “Leadership reporting” with “Executive dashboarding” or “Leadership decision support” for sharper phrasing.
- If accurate, add one stronger optimization term such as “conversion analysis” or “content performance optimization.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Core Competencies: Analytics and reporting infrastructure” and “Technical + IT: Data, Analytics & Optimization.”
- Avoid repeating the exact same tool stack here and in Technical + IT; keep Topline Skills more strategic.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill cluster, but it reads generic and overlaps heavily with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies and several NACo bullets. Make it more senior, systems-oriented, and tied to delivery environments rather than basic tasks.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Broadcast, Studio & Event Production**
- Replace with tighter, higher-level terms: **Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and webcast operations • PTZ and multi-camera studio systems • Hybrid, virtual and in-person event delivery**
- If space allows, add an outcome-oriented qualifier: **Built and operated in-house studio and event production workflows**
- Avoid “video production and editing” unless editing is a hiring priority; it undersells the leadership/operations scope shown in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This duplicates Core Competencies: **“Multimedia production and livestream operations.”** Consider keeping the broader phrase there and using this item for more specific production systems.
- “Studio operations” and “hybrid and virtual event production” are already evidenced in the Director of Digital Media entry; don’t repeat the same wording verbatim.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too bare and duplicates the stronger “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” section. This item should either be tightened to emphasize depth in the most relevant platforms or broadened only where it adds distinct value.

Suggested edit:
- Prioritize by depth/relevance: “Drupal (expert) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages”
- If space allows, add scope rather than just names: “Drupal (enterprise migrations, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages”
- Consider renaming to “CMS & Web Platforms” for cleaner phrasing and consistency with the rest of the CV.
- If GitHub Pages was only lightly used, replace it with a more substantive platform/tool or remove it.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution,” which already lists the same core platforms plus broader technical context.
- Drupal is already strongly evidenced in recent roles; avoid repeating it elsewhere without adding level, scale, or specialization.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but this item reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize implementation depth and newer tools that support recent work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Technical Implementation: HTML/CSS/JavaScript • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
- Drop versioning (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless used elsewhere consistently; it adds little value.
- Consider grouping by function for clarity: Front-end: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery | Integration/Deployment: APIs, GitHub Actions | Tagging/Edge: GTM, Cloudflare Workers
- If accurate, add scope/outcome context elsewhere in experience bullets, e.g., “implemented GTM and API-based workflows” or “used Cloudflare Workers/GitHub Actions to streamline deployment and site functionality.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the exact phrasing in both places.
- GTM may fit better under Analytics/Optimization if space is tight.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as an undifferentiated software list and overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Workflow automation / Airtable systems” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize systems you actually used to build automation and coordination workflows.

Suggested edit:
- Split by function and lead with higher-value automation tools: “Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier | Jira • Asana • Trello | Slack • Teams”
- Consider renaming to “Automation, Project & Collaboration Tools” so the category matches the contents more accurately.
- Drop lower-signal or older tools unless they are important for target roles; Basecamp is the easiest cut.
- If space allows elsewhere, convert this from a pure list into evidence: e.g., “Built workflow systems in Airtable, Power Automate and Zapier; managed cross-team delivery in Jira/Asana/Trello.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills.
- Slack/Teams are generic collaboration tools and may add little unless grouped more strategically.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful tools to include, but this line is too bare compared with the rest of the CV and doesn’t reflect the scale of your email leadership in recent roles. It should emphasize enterprise email/engagement platforms rather than read like a generic software list.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms
- Reorder by likely relevance/recency: Higher Logic • Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Mailchimp
- If accurate, add scope in a compact way: Higher Logic (enterprise/member communications) • Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys (journey automation) • Mailchimp (campaign email)
- Keep product names consistent and concise; consider shortening “Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys” to “Dynamics 365 Customer Insights (Journeys)” for readability

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Your work experience already shows strong email leadership; don’t repeat newsletter scale or audience size here unless you remove it from role bullets.
- “Engagement” overlaps with “Multi-channel communications operations” in Core Competencies, so keep this item tool-focused, not strategic.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization” and the NACo director bullet about expanding analytics infrastructure. Use it to sharpen technical specificity, not repeat themes already proven elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Analytics & Optimization Tools
- Tighten to a cleaner tool stack: GA4 • BigQuery • Looker Studio • Power BI • Microsoft Clarity • Google Search Console • Google Optimize / A/B testing tools
- Replace vague nouns like “Dashboarding” with a platform or capability: KPI reporting dashboards or dashboard design
- If accurate, add one higher-signal capability instead of a generic term: event tracking strategy, conversion analysis, SEO performance analysis, or experimentation

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “SEO” and “A/B testing” read as broad competencies, not tools; they fit better in Topline Skills than Technical + IT unless paired with specific platforms.
- This item duplicates the Topline Skills analytics list almost exactly; consider consolidating or making this version strictly tool-based.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is still broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more foundational and execution-focused, with concrete outputs or scale if you can add them.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize early-team building and hands-on production: “Promoted across two digital roles to help establish NACo’s first in-house digital team and improve execution across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Add clearer scope/results: mention website refresh scale, livestream/event volume, video cadence, or audience reach if available.
- Tighten the second sentence to focus on outputs: “Supported a major website refresh, produced livestreams and weekly video updates, and helped standardize day-to-day digital workflows.”
- Replace “providing day-to-day guidance” with a stronger management phrase if accurate: “mentored” or “supervised” a digital media associate.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; keep this entry focused on launching/building the capability rather than expanding it.
- “strengthening workflows” is repeated across multiple roles; specify what changed or what systems/processes were introduced.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads broadly and undersells the most distinctive achievement: launching NACo’s first podcast. Since later roles already cover digital/media growth, this item should emphasize foundational innovation, research support, and first-of-its-kind multimedia work.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to lead with the strongest outcome: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting county-focused programs and policy priorities.”
- Make the podcast achievement more concrete and concise: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting and production.”
- Tighten the digital content line to show support role without overlapping later jobs: “Produced digital and multimedia content to support program communications and research dissemination.”
- If accurate, add scope or output: number of projects supported, episodes produced, or audiences/stakeholders served.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid broad phrases like “digital content production and multimedia materials,” which overlap with later digital media roles.
- Don’t overstate leadership in digital operations here; save team/channel ownership for 2015 onward roles.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong supporting skills, but this item is partly redundant with “Multimedia Production & Event Delivery” and reads more like a mix of software and capabilities. Tightening it to named tools will make the section cleaner and more scannable.

Suggested edit:
- Rename or refocus as software/tools only: “Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator”
- If you want to keep capabilities, split them: “Multimedia & Creative Tools: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator” and move “Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production” to a capabilities section.
- Consider adding level/scope only if defensible, e.g., “Adobe Premiere Pro, Audition, Photoshop, Illustrator” for cleaner branding consistency.
- If these tools were used recently in leadership roles, you could sharpen with one qualifier: “Adobe Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Broadcast studio production”
